geometries.name: wigley_hull
geometries.title: Wigley parabolic hull
geometries.description: The analytic Wigley hull y = (B/2)(1 - (2x/L)^2)(1 - (z/T)^2) below the waterline, continued wall-sided up to a flat deck at the freeboard: a closed solid (Cb = 4/9). The classic ITTC benchmark for wave resistance, sinkage / trim and potential-flow / RANS free-surface codes.
geometries.frame: right-handed, metres: x aft, y to starboard, z up; origin at midships on the centre plane in the calm waterline (bow at x = -L/2, stern at x = +L/2, keel at z = -T)
physics: wave resistance and wave pattern (Michell thin-ship theory, Rankine panels)
RANS / VOF free-surface CFD validation (resistance, sinkage and trim)
seakeeping: heave / pitch response in head waves
mesh-convergence benchmark for hull CFD

sources.what: parabolic waterlines and frames y = (B/2)(1-(2x/L)^2)(1-(z/T)^2)
sources.ref: Wigley, W.C.S. (1934). A comparison of experiment and calculated wave-profiles and wave-resistances for a form having parabolic waterlines. Proc. Royal Society of London A 144(851), 144-159. https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1934.0040

sources.what: benchmark proportions L/B = 10, B/T = 1.6
sources.ref: Kajitani, H., Miyata, H., Ikehata, M., Tanaka, H., Adachi, H., Namimatsu, M., Ogiwara, S. (1983). The summary of the cooperative experiment on Wigley parabolic model in Japan. Proc. 2nd DTNSRDC Workshop on Ship Wave-Resistance Computations, Bethesda, 5-35 (ITTC Resistance Committee benchmark, L/B = 10, B/T = 1.6)

sources.what: default L = 1 m (non-dimensional reference) and freeboard 0.04 L, wall-sided above the waterline
sources.ref: choice for a normalised closed solid

geometries.regenerate:
import pinneapple as pp
g = pp.geometries.build("wigley_hull", lod="light")
g.export("wigley_hull.glb")

geometries.name: wind_turbine_nrel5mw
geometries.title: NREL 5-MW reference wind turbine
geometries.description: Three-bladed upwind 5-MW turbine: blades lofted through the published chord / twist table with a cylinder-to-airfoil root transition, 2.5 deg precone, 5 deg shaft tilt, hub with spinner, nacelle and tapered tower (onshore, base at z = 0). Rotor azimuth, blade pitch and yaw-free geometry for rotor CFD (actuator line / sliding mesh), wake and loads studies.
geometries.frame: right-handed, metres: x downwind, y lateral, z up; origin at the tower base on the ground; rotor upwind of the tower (x < 0)
physics: rotor aerodynamics (BEM, actuator line, blade-resolved CFD)
wake and wind-farm interaction
aeroelastic blade loads
tower shadow, icing, erosion of the leading edge

sources.what: rotor 126 m, hub 3 m, hub height 90 m, precone 2.5 deg, shaft tilt 5 deg, overhang 5 m, blade chord / twist / airfoil table, tower 6 m -> 3.87 m over 87.6 m
sources.ref: Jonkman, J., Butterfield, S., Musial, W., Scott, G. (2009). Definition of a 5-MW Reference Wind Turbine for Offshore System Development. NREL/TP-500-38060. https://doi.org/10.2172/947422

sources.what: airfoil shapes: the DU 40/35/30/25/21 and NACA 64-618 sections are approximated by NACA 4-digit sections with the same thickness ratio and 2-4 % camber
sources.ref: approximation (coordinates of the DU sections are not reproduced)

sources.what: bounding box: 109.3 m wide because at azimuth 0 the blades point up and at +-120 deg (2 R sin 120 deg), 152.5 m high (hub 90 m + R cos(precone))
sources.ref: model geometry

sources.what: nacelle 14 x 3.8 x 3.9 m and spinner shape
sources.ref: estimates from 5-MW-class nacelles
